pr_title: fix: incorrect super type for literals in nested binary exprs
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/12227.

There was a match block that unconditionally gave priority to the non-literal side for the case when one side was a literal and the other was not, which became incorrect when the type of the `Literal` was the super type.

This fix adds an additional check to make it so that the type of the `Literal` is ignored only when both sides are integer types.

issue_context.title: result dtype of expr with comparison operation wrongly promoted as int
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame().select(x=pl.Series([1]))
y = (0.1 * (pl.col('x') > 0))
print(df.with_columns(y=y, y_error=+y))
```

### Log output

```shell
shape: (1, 3)
┌─────┬─────┬─────────┐
│ x   ┆ y   ┆ y_error │
│ --- ┆ --- ┆ ---     │
│ i64 ┆ f64 ┆ i32     │
╞═════╪═════╪═════════╡
│ 1   ┆ 0.1 ┆ 0       │
└─────┴─────┴─────────┘
```


### Issue description

the result dtype of expr  like `+(0.1 * (pl.col('x') > 0))` is wrongly promoted as int.

### Expected behavior

the expected result dtype is float.

comments:
Triage / further-simplifying the MWE (it's connected to the `pl.lit(0)` implicitly applied by unary plus):
```python
df = pl.select( x=pl.Series([1]) )
df.select( y=pl.lit(0) + ((pl.col('x') > 0) * 0.1) )

# shape: (1, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ y   │
# │ --- │
# │ i32 │
# ╞═════╡
# │ 0   │
# └─────┘
```

review_comments: Instead of removing this whole functionality, can we branch this under numerical types? When dealing with numerical types, it is wasteful to upcast a whole column to a literal.
yeah, I think that's a good idea - have updated to branch under integer types.
